C0.quote: IRV has a moderating effect relative to plurality voting
C0.note: Compares the winners of two voting rules, IRV and plurality, on a 1-D Euclidean model.

C1.quote: if there is a candidate in [1/6, 5/6], then the IRV winner is in [1/6, 5/6]
C1.note: Main results are theorems on exclusion zones, a property of a rule; simulations only validate them. Probabilistic winner-distribution results are also theorems. No welfare or distortion criterion is used.

C2.1.value: rankings (voters submit a ranking over the candidates)
C2.1.quote: voters submit a ranking over the candidates

C2.2.quote: IRV elections ask voters to rank candidates in order of preference
C2.2.note: Full strict rankings; truncated ballots are mentioned only as future work.

C2.3.quote: voters form preferences over candidates by ranking them in order of proximity
C2.3.note: Voters have ideological positions on [0,1] and 1-Euclidean preferences.

C2.4.quote: Voters prefer candidates closer to them (i.e., they have 1-Euclidean preferences)
C2.4.note: Rankings are derived directly from positions and the rule is applied to them. The paper never states that submitted rankings equal held preferences.

C3.1.quote: we did not consider strategic analyses
C3.1.note: No analysis has voters misreport. Candidate strategy is also excluded.

C3.2.note: Sincere voting is never stated in words. Voters simply vote for or rank by proximity.

C4.1.note: No voter utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: The criterion is moderation of the winner's position, which is not among the listed criteria. Metric distortion and representation are mentioned only as other literature.

VOT.quote_behav: the fraction of voters who vote for candidate xi is the probability mass
VOT.note: Voters vote for or rank by proximity; their behaviour is fixed by the model.

CAN.quote_behav: we do not analyze strategic choices by candidates
CAN.note: Candidates are random or fixed positions serving only as alternatives.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: we prove that IRV has a moderating effect relative to plurality voting
IRV will push out more extreme candidates

C9.1.note: Claims bear on the real-world debate over adopting IRV versus plurality, but no explicit recommendation of a rule is made.

C9.2.quote: voters favor candidates who are closer to them on the line
C9.2.note: The real-world moderation claim needs voters to submit their held proximity rankings (sincerity), which is not stated. The 1-D preference structure and non-strategic candidates are stated.
